column3: NASB renders “child” as “son.”
NASB renders “among many witnesses” as “in the presence of many witnesses” and “sufficient” as “able.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Suffer hardship with me”) without the Textus Receptus “You therefore.”
NASB adds “in active service” and “as a soldier,” and renders “the affairs of this life” as “the affairs of everyday life.”
NASB adds “as an athlete” and renders “is crowned” as “win the prize” and “lawfully” as “according to the rules.”
NASB renders “to partake first of the fruits” as “to be the first to receive his share of the crops.”
NASB follows the critical text (“will give”).
NASB renders “raised” as “risen” and “from the seed of David” as “descendant of David.”
NASB renders “chains” as “imprisonment,” “evildoer” as “criminal,” and “has not been bound” as “is not imprisoned.”
NASB renders “the elect” as “those who are chosen” and adds “and with it.”
NASB renders “saying” as “statement.” A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB renders “we will deny” as “we deny.”
NASB follows the critical text (“for”).
NASB follows the critical text (“God”); it renders “quarrel about words” as “wrangle about words” and “subversion” as “ruin.”
NASB renders “hasten” as “Be diligent” and “not ashamed” as “who does not need to be ashamed.”
NASB renders “babblings” as “chatter” and “on to more” as “to further.”
NASB renders “will have pasture to grow” as “will spread.”
NASB renders “are overthrowing” as “upset” and adds “thus.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the Lord”); it puts the two sayings in quotation marks and renders “iniquity” as “wickedness.” Stray spacing around the quotation marks appears in the NASB text.
NASB adds “vessels” and renders “great” as “large.”
NASB follows the critical text without “and.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “breed” as “produce.”
NASB renders “gentle” as “kind” and “forbearing” as “patient when wronged.”
NASB renders “disciplining” as “correcting” and “otherwise” as “if perhaps.”
NASB renders “recover” as “come to their senses and escape” and adds “to do”; who is meant by “his will” is uncertain.
